data.title: Iontophoresis unit
data.summary: Cryo / electro / light devices · Galvanic device that drives charged drug ions or tap-water ions into skin with direct current.
data.body:
_Also called: Iontophoresis_

Galvanic device that drives charged drug ions or tap-water ions into skin with direct current.

## Parts
- DC source with current control (0-3.8 mA)
- Treating and indifferent electrodes
- Trays/pads

## Uses / indications
- Palmoplantar hyperhidrosis
- Drug delivery: tretinoin (scars), glycolic acid, retinoids for melasma, sodium salicylate (warts), zinc oxide (ulcer), iodide (scars), idoxuridine (herpes labialis)
- Patch testing, pilocarpine (sweat) test

## Contraindications
- Anaesthetic skin
- Cuts, wounds, ulcers
- Dermatitis

## Method of use
1. Clean area with spirit
2. Khopkar: for acidic agents the cathode is the treating electrode and the anode indifferent; reverse for alkaline agents
3. Raise current slowly 0-3.8 mA with continuous circular/stroking movement of the electrode; full face takes about 20-25 min
4. End point mild erythema; reduce to zero and reverse polarity briefly

## Viva points & tips
- Physics: like charges repel - cations are driven from the anode, anions from the cathode (Khopkar's principle sentence labels acidic agents as cations repelled by the cathode - verify)
- Grease abrasions; stop and reverse current if pain/burning
- Complications: erythema, urticaria, burns, irritant/allergic dermatitis
